Invocation C withheld two archives, so its graph is not an all-JAR graph. The two withholding reasons recorded under 'withheld' below are witness-preservation reasons measured at the time; they are recorded as what was done, not as a licence to trim the mandated input. delivery_evidence_for_the_graph_the_runn.why_this_node_was_added: QA Issue 7 (HIGH): the ordered manifest above is the delivery evidence of invocation C, whose staging directory sat in the w-000 checkout and is not on this host any more. Of its 189 entries only 61 resolve to a file in this checkout's reach, so as delivery evidence for anything a reader can check it had lapsed. AAP 0.5.1 makes the logged one-to-one manifest -- 'not a per-module class search' -- the proof that every archive was supplied to the frontend, so that proof has to exist for the graph the runners and the probe ACTUALLY load. This node is that proof, re-derived first-hand against the staging tree that graph was built from. Nothing above was deleted: invocation C's manifest remains exactly as published, because it is still an accurate record OF INVOCATION C.

the_mutability_hazard_this_node_exists_b.what_that_means: the staging tree is hard-linked into /opt/spark-src rather than copied, exactly as cpg-record.txt line 8 says ('staged as hard links'). A staged archive and the reactor artifact it came from are ONE inode, so a rebuild of the pinned tree rewrites the frontend's recorded inputs in place, under a manifest that still states the old bytes.
the_mutability_hazard_this_node_exists_b.observed_consequence: three archives had drifted between the 2026-09-02 measurement and 2026-09-03: common_utils__original-spark-common-utils_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar (511,979 -> 511,981 bytes, digest 38627c49... -> 3e915222...), common_utils__spark-common-utils_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar (517,232 -> 517,234 bytes, digest ebeca6c4... -> f16f1273...) and common_network-yarn__spark-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT-yarn-shuffle.jar (109,208,027 bytes unchanged, digest ab5f23f6... -> 5fb2b39a...). QA reproduced the same signature against invocation C's manifest.
the_mutability_hazard_this_node_exists_b.why_it_was_not_fixed_by_re_staging: staging by copy is the correct fix and it belongs to provisioning: /opt/blitzy-harness/cpg-input is shared read-only across clones, and re-staging it from a scan run would change what every sibling clone measures mid-flight. This run does the half that is its own -- re-derive and republish the manifest against the tree as it stands, in the same act as the graph re-anchor -- and names the other half as a provisioning change.
the_mutability_hazard_this_node_exists_b.what_a_reader_should_do: treat this node's digests as of 2026-09-03T09:33Z and re-measure before relying on them, because the inodes remain shared.

what_this_node_does_NOT_establish.aap_0_5_1_all_jar_coverage: This input set is 62 archives from 31 modules. The reactor has 38 JAR-packaging projects, and 7 of them contributed no archive to it (connector/kafka-0-10, connector/kafka-0-10-assembly, connector/kafka-0-10-sql, connector/kafka-0-10-token-provider, examples, sql/connect/shims, tools -- enumerated in cpg-input-inventory.json and in cpg-module-coverage.json). So this graph is NOT the all-JAR graph AAP 0.5.1 mandates, and this node must not be read as claiming it is.
what_this_node_does_NOT_establish.why_the_shortfall_stands: closing it requires a new frontend build over all 38 projects' artifacts, which is a rebuild of a host-shared graph this run may not perform. It is published as a named limitation rather than silently satisfied.
